headline: Banks failed across Europe, Japan took Manchuria, and Chaplin opened a silent picture four years into sound
texture: City Lights opened in Los Angeles on January 30, silent apart from a synchronized score, four years after The Jazz Singer. It took $2,000,000 in domestic rentals, more than any other release that year. Rentals are the distributor share rather than the ticket window total, so the figure is roughly half of what a modern gross would report. Universal put out Dracula on February 14 and Frankenstein in New York on November 21. Cimarron won Outstanding Production at the Biltmore Hotel on November 10.

Creditanstalt, the largest bank in Austria, went under on May 11 and took the Central European banking system with it. Britain left the gold standard on September 19. Record sales had been $75 million in 1929 and came to $5.5 million this year, so companies stopped signing new acts and recorded the ones who already sold. Food riots broke out in Minneapolis in February. Al Capone was sentenced to eleven years on October 17, for tax evasion rather than for anything else he had done.

Japanese officers staged an explosion near Mukden on September 18, blamed it on Chinese dissidents, and took Manchuria. Spain became a republic on April 14 and approved its constitution on December 9. The Empire State Building was finished on May 1 and the George Washington Bridge was dedicated on October 24. The Star-Spangled Banner became the national anthem on March 3, and Nevada legalized gambling two weeks after that. Clara, Lu, and Em went out on NBC Blue on January 27, the first daytime serial on radio.

pol.us_president.label: US President
pol.us_president.detail: Third year of his term, with Charles Curtis as vice president and Charles Evans Hughes as chief justice.

pol.us_congress.label: US Congress
pol.us_congress.detail: Nicholas Longworth (R) was Speaker until March 4. John Nance Garner (D) took the chair when the new Congress finally sat on December 7. James Eli Watson (R) led the Senate.

pol.anthem.label: The Star-Spangled Banner adopted
pol.anthem.value: Became the US national anthem by act of Congress

pol.capone.label: Al Capone sentenced
pol.capone.value: Eleven years in prison for tax evasion

pol.scottsboro.label: Scottsboro Boys arrested
pol.scottsboro.value: Arrested in Alabama and charged with a sexual offence

pol.prohibition.label: Prohibition
pol.prohibition.value: Still in force, in its twelfth year since 1920

world.uk_pm.label: UK Prime Minister
world.uk_pm.detail: His Labour government resigned on August 24 and he stayed on to lead a National Government, which won the general election on October 27.

world.creditanstalt.label: Creditanstalt collapse
world.creditanstalt.value: Austria's largest bank went bankrupt, starting the Central European banking collapse

world.manchuria.label: Mukden Incident
world.manchuria.value: Japanese officers staged an explosion, blamed Chinese dissidents, and occupied Manchuria
world.manchuria.detail: Held at gunpoint, the Chinese commander of Kirin province announced the province's annexation two days later.

world.spain.label: Second Spanish Republic
world.spain.value: Proclaimed in Madrid after April municipal elections were treated as a referendum on the monarchy
world.spain.detail: The Cortes approved a constitution on December 9 and elected Niceto Alcala-Zamora president the next day.

world.china_flood.label: China floods
world.china_flood.value: The Yangtze and Huai rivers flooded a densely populated region from June to November

world.statute_westminster.label: Statute of Westminster
world.statute_westminster.value: Parliament gave the self-governing dominions legislative equality with Britain

world.empire_state.label: Empire State Building completed
world.empire_state.detail: The George Washington Bridge over the Hudson was dedicated on October 24.

film.gross.label: Highest-grossing films, US domestic rentals
value: The Man Who Came Back, $1,400,000, Fox
film.gross.detail: Rentals, meaning the distributor share rather than the ticket window total. Sources for this period disagree by roughly a factor of two, and a rentals figure is about half what a gross figure would say.

film.best_picture.label: Outstanding Production
film.best_picture.detail: The 4th Academy Awards were held at the Biltmore Hotel in Los Angeles on November 10, for films released between August 1930 and July 1931. Norman Taurog won Best Director for Skippy, Lionel Barrymore Best Actor and Marie Dressler Best Actress. Cimarron was the first Western to win.

film.world_cinema.label: Notable international releases
value: A Nous la Liberte, Rene Clair (France)

film.how_people_watched.label: How people watched
film.how_people_watched.value: In a theatre, and nowhere else. City Lights premiered on January 30 as a silent picture with a synchronized score, four years after sound arrived.

radio.debuts.label: New on the air
value: Clara, Lu, and Em, January 27 on NBC Blue, the first daytime serial
The Fred Waring Show, January 4 on NBC
The Witch's Tale, May 21 on WOR
Metropolitan Opera Saturday matinees, December 25 on NBC Blue

music.recordings.label: Records people bought
value: Good-night Sweetheart, Wayne King and His Orchestra
Mood Indigo, Duke Ellington and His Cotton Club Orchestra
Sweet and Lovely, Gus Arnheim's Cocoanut Grove Orchestra
music.recordings.detail: There was no Billboard chart in 1931. This ordering comes from Joel Whitburn's Pop Memories, compiled from sales reported decades later, so treat the ranking as approximate.

music.format.label: The record business
music.format.value: Sales fell from $75 million in 1929 to $18 million in 1930 and $5.5 million this year
music.format.detail: A top-selling record took $500,000 or more in 1929, under $100,000 in 1930, and about $60,000 this year. Labels stopped taking chances on new acts and recorded the ones who already sold.

culture.mood.label: Mood
culture.mood.value: The second full year after the crash, with banks going down in Europe, food riots in American cities, and no bottom in sight to anyone standing in it.

sports.world_series.label: World Series
sports.world_series.value: St. Louis Cardinals beat the Philadelphia Athletics, four games to three
sports.world_series.detail: Played October 1 to 10. Frankie Frisch and Lefty Grove took the league MVP awards.

sports.nfl.label: NFL champions
sports.nfl.value: Green Bay Packers, 12 wins and 2 losses
sports.nfl.detail: There was no championship game yet. The title went on the regular season record.

sports.negro_league.label: Negro National League disbands
sports.negro_league.value: The St. Louis Stars won the final championship before the league folded

deaths.edison.label: Thomas Edison
deaths.edison.detail: He had filed his last patent application in January.

deaths.rockne.label: Knute Rockne
deaths.rockne.value: Died March 31 in a plane crash, aged 43

deaths.michelson.label: Albert A. Michelson
deaths.michelson.detail: Physicist and Nobel laureate, born in Germany.

notes: Research pass July 2026. The prices, television and technology sections are empty on purpose. Gas, minimum wage and ticket price series all start later than 1931, and no free primary source gives a 1931 unemployment rate, so nothing numeric is claimed rather than reaching for a secondary estimate. Records are reported without a chart position because there was no Billboard chart until 1940. Box office is rentals, which is what the source says, and the amounts are labelled as the distributor share.
